answer: A time-locked gate works like a meadow with a single narrow inlet: every new identity must first complete a verifiable delay function, a computation that takes hours of sequential work and cannot be sped up by adding machines. A jade seal is issued only when the delay proof checks out, so each fake identity costs real wall-clock time. An attacker wanting ten thousand Sybils would need ten thousand sequential delays, while one honest agent waits once and is done.
